WAKE GOVERNANCE
=================

This module is the mechanical authority between untrusted proposals and durable
state. Intelligence may suggest a transition. Only these deterministic rules
decide whether the transition is permitted.

The separation is the kernel's central trust boundary:

    provider output  = untrusted proposal
    governance       = deterministic permission
    replay           = accepted state transition
    record           = durable evidence

Governance never calls a model, interprets persuasive prose, or changes policy
based on the provider that submitted a proposal. Given the same state, revision,
and proposal, it must return the same decision.

Evaluation is whole-proposal atomic. If any operation is stale, malformed,
duplicated, or invalid for the current lifecycle, the complete proposal is
rejected. We do not partially accept the safe-looking operations because doing
so would create state the proposer never observed or intended as a standalone
transition.

Rejection is expected product behavior, not exceptional corruption. A rejected
proposal becomes a hash-linked receipt while authoritative state and revision
remain unchanged. This lets failure teach future disposable invocations without
letting failure become accepted state.

Rules in this module validate whether a change may happen. They must not mutate
state. Record replay owns how an accepted action changes state. Whenever an
action is added, its models, governance, replay, proof, and presentation must be
updated together.
"""

{"requested_url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/46bddc182cda2d875a98c0e4bfda7af25acf50fc/docs/architecture.md", "source_revision": "46bddc182cda2d875a98c0e4bfda7af25acf50fc", "running_revision": "8e6574128486bc628b98e8b43e90544bd0d50569", "source_search": "", "url": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudofx/wake/46bddc182cda2d875a98c0e4bfda7af25acf50fc/docs/architecture.md", "scope": "raw source-controlled WAKE repository text", "excerpt": "# Architecture and limits

See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**.
